svg.title: The finite Cartan identity determines the action
svg.desc: The holonomic pair plane Lambda in the determining-jet and equation-jet fibre product maps by d sigma j to the next equation plane. The inductive point-action formula gives the same plane. Together with the same lower jet, plane injectivity forces equality of the next jets. Full action morphisms, stabilizer schemes and orbit symbols agree, so the one finite-level Lie-Tresse domain applies.

g.text: A finite Cartan identity determines the actual jet action
Given: σⱼ : Gʲ ×_M Eʲ → Eʲ, with the specified base M and σ₀.
Gʲ ⊂ Dʲ(M); finite order, FI, algebraic fixed-point groups. No action formula prescribed.
Pair the two holonomic planes by their common source vector.
Induction and the transformed-graph chain rule also give L(g⁽ʲ⁺¹⁾e).
Same lower jet + same holonomic plane ⇒ same next jet.
Thus σⱼ(g,e)=g⁽ʲ⁾e at every finite order. Proof: Theorem 4.45.
Equality of action morphisms, including every group component
⇒ full stabilizer schemes, tangent kernels, orbit tangents Δⱼ and symbols ϖⱼ agree.
The reduced product point test gives scheme equality, not only infinitesimal equality.
∃ L and invariant U⊂Eᴸ: every point of every complete higher inverse image is covered.
A_L = F_L[∇^α f_b : |α|>0]; affine quotients and finite/formal geometric separation.
